components.note: 氵 (water) — water and liquids, as in 河, 海, 汤: clear water.
青 (qīng) gives the exact sound; also 请 qǐng, 情 qíng, 晴 qíng and 精 jīng.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 周末我们要清理一下车库。
example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen yào qīnglǐ yíxià chēkù.
example.english: This weekend we need to clean out the garage.
example.fact: 清理 combines 清 ("clear, clean") with 理 ("to sort, to manage") to describe organizing and removing clutter, a step further than 打扫, which is closer to plain "sweeping."

examples.hanzi: 请把桌子上的东西清理一下。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhuōzi shang de dōngxi qīnglǐ yíxià.
examples.english: Please tidy up the things on the table.

examples.hanzi: 工人正在清理街上的雪。
examples.pinyin: Gōngrén zhèngzài qīnglǐ jiē shang de xuě.
examples.english: Workers are clearing the snow off the street.

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: voices in unison. 同 also gives sound to 铜 tóng, 桶 tǒng, 洞 dòng.

example.hanzi: 这两个答案完全相同。
example.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè dá'àn wánquán xiāngtóng.
example.english: These two answers are exactly the same.
example.fact: 相同 is the formal, written-register counterpart of the everyday 一样 — reports and textbooks favor 相同 (与...相同, 相同的结果), while casual speech reaches for 跟...一样 instead.

examples.hanzi: 我们的想法完全相同。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de xiǎngfǎ wánquán xiāngtóng.
examples.english: Our ideas are exactly the same.

examples.hanzi: 这对双胞胎长得几乎相同。
examples.pinyin: Zhè duì shuāngbāotāi zhǎng de jīhū xiāngtóng.
examples.english: The twins look almost identical.

components.note: 阝 (mound, steps) — left-side 阝 is 阜 (mound or steps), as in 阶, 院, 阳; 陛 is the steps up to a throne.
坒 (bì) — same sound — 陛 is bì, as in 陛下 Your Majesty.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 大臣们跪下说:“陛下万岁!”
example.pinyin: Dàchénmen guìxià shuō: “Bìxià wànsuì!”
example.english: The ministers knelt and said, "Long live Your Majesty!"
example.fact: 陛 originally referred to the steps leading up to a throne, so 陛下 literally means "below the steps [of the throne]" — a term of address built, like English "Your Highness," around the speaker's position relative to the monarch rather than a direct name for the ruler.

examples.hanzi: 国王对大臣说:“陛下,请您放心。”
examples.pinyin: Guówáng duì dàchén shuō: "Bìxià, qǐng nín fàngxīn."
examples.english: The minister said to the king, "Your Majesty, please rest assured."

examples.hanzi: 陛下,客人已经到了。
examples.pinyin: Bìxià, kèrén yǐjīng dào le.
examples.english: Your Majesty, the guests have arrived.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室; 完 first meant complete, whole.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; 元 also sounds out 玩 wán, 院 yuàn and 远 yuǎn.
比 (bǐ) — near sound — 毕 is bì; 比 also sounds out 毙 bì, so the shared syllable bì is easy to remember.

example.hanzi: 会议已经完毕,大家可以回家了。
example.pinyin: Huìyì yǐjīng wánbì, dàjiā kěyǐ huí jiā le.
example.english: The meeting has ended — everyone can go home now.
example.fact: 完毕 is a formal way of saying "finished," often heard in announcements or procedural reports ("报告完毕," roughly "over and out") — everyday speech prefers 完了 or 结束.

examples.hanzi: 这份报告我已经写完毕了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fèn bàogào wǒ yǐjīng xiě wánbì le.
examples.english: I've already finished writing this report.

examples.hanzi: 手续办理完毕后,你就可以回去了。
examples.pinyin: Shǒuxù bànlǐ wánbì hòu, nǐ jiù kěyǐ huíqù le.
examples.english: After the procedures are completed, you can go back.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — vessels and containers: 盘, 盆, 盖, 益; 血 is a drop 丿 in a bowl: blood.
氵 (water) — 氵 is water and liquids, as in 海, 汤, 酒; 液 is a liquid.
夜 (yè) — same sound — 液 is yè, like 夜 night.

example.hanzi: 医生检查了他的血液。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng jiǎnchá le tā de xuèyè.
example.english: The doctor examined his blood.
example.fact: 血液 is the clinical, formal term for blood (as in 血液类型, "blood type"), while the single character 血 is what everyday speech and compounds like 流血 ("to bleed") normally use.

examples.hanzi: 他今天要去医院验血液。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān yào qù yīyuàn yàn xuèyè.
examples.english: He's going to the hospital today for a blood test.

examples.hanzi: 血液在身体里不停地流动。
examples.pinyin: Xuèyè zài shēntǐ lǐ bù tíng de liúdòng.
examples.english: Blood keeps flowing through the body.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 脑, 脚, 肚; here part of the simplified form 胜 for victory.
生 (shēng) is a near sound match for shèng; also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.

example.hanzi: 我们队以三比一获胜。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen duì yǐ sān bǐ yī huòshèng.
example.english: Our team won three to one.
example.fact: 胜 is to win: 胜利 (victory), 战胜 (to overcome), 获胜 (to win). It also means to surpass: 一个比一个强, 胜于. 名胜 means a famous scenic spot, and 数不胜数 means countless.

examples.hanzi: 这场比赛谁能获胜？
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng bǐsài shéi néng huòshèng?
examples.english: Who will win this match?

examples.hanzi: 这次胜利很不容易。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì shènglì hěn bù róngyì.
examples.english: This victory wasn't easy.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — 竹 (bamboo) as in 笔, 筷, 篮; boxes and baskets were woven from bamboo, so 箱 is a box or chest.
相 (xiāng) — same sound — 箱 is xiāng, just like 相.

example.hanzi: 请把行李放进箱子里。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ xíngli fàng jìn xiāngzi lǐ.
example.english: Please put the luggage in the box.
example.fact: 箱 makes many container words: 冰箱 (fridge), 行李箱 (suitcase), 信箱 (mailbox), 邮箱 (email inbox, or an email address). 箱子 is the general word for a box or suitcase.

examples.hanzi: 冰箱里有一个小箱子。
examples.pinyin: Bīngxiāng lǐ yǒu yí gè xiǎo xiāngzi.
examples.english: There is a small box in the fridge.

examples.hanzi: 他提着一个大行李箱。
examples.pinyin: Tā tízhe yí gè dà xínglǐxiāng.
examples.english: He is carrying a big suitcase.

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
乛 (hook stroke) — the top-left bent stroke and dictionary radical; a stroke grouping with no meaning of its own.
一 (one) — the bottom bar. 卫 is simplified from 衛 (guard); Memory aid: a bar blocking a corner, a guard at the door.

example.hanzi: 大卫每天都去健身房。
example.pinyin: Dàwèi měitiān dōu qù jiànshēnfáng.
example.english: David goes to the gym every day.
example.fact: Like 比尔, 大卫 is a phonetic transliteration of an English name chosen for sound rather than sense — though 卫 ("to guard, to defend") happens to echo the biblical David's role as a warrior-king, a coincidence rather than a deliberate translation.

examples.hanzi: 大卫是我大学时最好的朋友。
examples.pinyin: Dàwèi shì wǒ dàxué shí zuì hǎo de péngyou.
examples.english: David was my best friend in college.

examples.hanzi: 你认识大卫吗?他在银行工作。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ rènshi Dàwèi ma? Tā zài yínháng gōngzuò.
examples.english: Do you know David? He works at a bank.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.
女 (woman) — women and family terms, as in 妈 mom, 好 good, 姐 sister; 女 (nǚ) also loosely echoes the rú sound.
口 (mouth) — speech; 如 originally meant "to follow, accord with", later "as, like"; also in 汝 rǔ and 茹 rú.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们; 何 was a person carrying a load (荷 hè).
可 (kě) is a close sound clue for hé; also in 河 hé, 歌 gē and 哥 gē.

example.hanzi: 无论如何,我都会支持你。
example.pinyin: Wúlùn rúhé, wǒ dōu huì zhīchí nǐ.
example.english: No matter what, I will support you.
example.fact: 无论如何 belongs to a family of 无论 + question-word constructions (无论谁, 无论什么, 无论怎样) that all mean "no matter ___" — 如何 here means "how," so the literal sense is closer to "regardless of how things turn out."

examples.hanzi: 无论如何,你都要按时吃药。
examples.pinyin: Wúlùn rúhé, nǐ dōu yào ànshí chī yào.
examples.english: Whatever happens, you must take your medicine on time.

examples.hanzi: 这件事无论如何我们也要做完。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wúlùn rúhé wǒmen yě yào zuòwán.
examples.english: We have to finish this no matter what.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — tasting and speaking: 吃, 喝, 嗅; 味 is flavor.
未 (wèi) sounds exactly like 味; also 妹 mèi.

example.hanzi: 这道菜的味道很好。
example.pinyin: Zhè dào cài de wèidào hěn hǎo.
example.english: This dish tastes very good.
example.fact: 味 means taste or smell, and 味道 covers both: 有味道 can mean "flavourful" or "smelly". It builds 口味 (taste preference) and 五味 (the five tastes). In traditional medicine 味 counts herbs: 一味药 (one ingredient).

examples.hanzi: 这个菜味道有点怪。
examples.pinyin: Zhège cài wèidào yǒudiǎn guài.
examples.english: This dish tastes a little strange.

examples.hanzi: 屋里有一股香味。
examples.pinyin: Wū lǐ yǒu yì gǔ xiāngwèi.
examples.english: There's a fragrant smell in the room.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
亻 (person) — person radical — 佑 is a person helping another.
右 (yòu) — same sound — 佑 is yòu, like 右; the right hand is the helping hand, as in 保佑.

example.hanzi: 老人常常祈求神明保佑全家平安。
example.pinyin: Lǎorén chángcháng qíqiú shénmíng bǎoyòu quán jiā píng'ān.
example.english: The elderly often pray to the gods to bless and protect the whole family, keeping everyone safe.
example.fact: 保佑 is used almost exclusively for protection from a divine or supernatural source (gods, ancestors, fate) — for protection by a person, law, or institution, Chinese uses 保护 instead.

examples.hanzi: 愿神明保佑你一路平安。
examples.pinyin: Yuàn shénmíng bǎoyòu nǐ yílù píng'ān.
examples.english: May the gods bless you with a safe journey.

examples.hanzi: 奶奶在寺庙里祈求保佑全家人健康。
examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zài sìmiào lǐ qíqiú bǎoyòu quán jiārén jiànkāng.
examples.english: Grandma prayed at the temple for her whole family's good health.

components.note: 重 (zhòng) is a sound clue for 种 zhǒng/zhòng; it means heavy (zhòng) or to repeat (chóng, as in 重新).
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 老师把这句话的重点画了出来。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ zhè jù huà de zhòngdiǎn huà le chūlái.
example.english: The teacher marked the key point of this sentence.
example.fact: 重点 uses the "heavy, important" reading of 重 (zhòng) — the same reading in 重要 ("important") and 严重 ("serious") — not the "repeat" reading chóng; literally, 重点 is "a weighty point."

examples.hanzi: 这次考试的重点是第三章。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì de zhòngdiǎn shì dì sān zhāng.
examples.english: The focus of this exam is chapter three.

examples.hanzi: 你说了这么多,但我没听出重点。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuō le zhème duō, dàn wǒ méi tīng chū zhòngdiǎn.
examples.english: You said so much, but I didn't catch the main point.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 事故发生时,他也在场。
example.pinyin: Shìgù fāshēng shí, tā yě zàichǎng.
example.english: He was also present when the accident happened.
example.fact: 在场 emphasizes physical presence at an event as it actually happens — an eyewitness sense — distinct from 出席, which is used for formally attending a scheduled event like a meeting or ceremony.

examples.hanzi: 昨天开会时,经理也在场。
examples.pinyin: Zuótiān kāihuì shí, jīnglǐ yě zàichǎng.
examples.english: The manager was also present at yesterday's meeting.

examples.hanzi: 当时在场的人都听到了他的话。
examples.pinyin: Dāngshí zàichǎng de rén dōu tīngdào le tā de huà.
examples.english: Everyone present at the time heard what he said.

components.note: 取 (qǔ, take) is the base; the loose sound clue also appears in 趣 qù and 娶 qǔ. The top 日 here is an old cap shape, not the sun.
高 (tall) — a drawing of a tall tower building. 高 also sounds out 糕 gāo (cake), 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.

example.hanzi: 珠穆朗玛峰是世界上最高的山。
example.pinyin: Zhūmùlǎngmǎ Fēng shì shìjiè shàng zuìgāo de shān.
example.english: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain in the world.
example.fact: 最 is the default superlative prefix in Mandarin and combines freely with almost any adjective — 最高, 最好, 最大 — without the irregular forms English superlatives sometimes need (like "good" becoming "best").

examples.hanzi: 这是我吃过的最高的蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ chī guo de zuì gāo de dàngāo.
examples.english: This is the tallest cake I've ever eaten.

examples.hanzi: 这座楼是城里最高的建筑。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò lóu shì chéng lǐ zuì gāo de jiànzhù.
examples.english: This building is the tallest in the city.

components.note: 雨 (rain) — weather, as in 雪 snow, 雷 thunder, 零 zero. Oldest form: a person waiting out rain; waiting turned into "need".
而 (ér) is only a loose sound hint here; 需 also sounds out 须 xū.

example.hanzi: 你需要帮助吗？
example.pinyin: Nǐ xūyào bāngzhù ma?
example.english: Do you need help?
example.fact: 需 is mostly in 需要 (to need, a need) and 需求 (demand). 需要 can act as a verb or a noun, unlike 要, which is a general "to want".

examples.hanzi: 你需要什么？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xūyào shénme?
examples.english: What do you need?

examples.hanzi: 这不需要太多钱。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù xūyào tài duō qián.
examples.english: This doesn't need much money.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
尸 (body/cover) — the top-left part, as in 局 and 层. Origin in 尉 is unclear; it is only a visible part.
寸 (inch/hand) — the right part and radical, as in 对 and 村. Memory aid: an officer with a hand on the order, as in 上尉 captain.

example.hanzi: 他二十八岁就晋升为上尉。
example.pinyin: Tā èrshíbā suì jiù jìnshēng wéi shàngwèi.
example.english: He was promoted to captain at just twenty-eight.
example.fact: 尉 is a rank suffix shared across a tier of junior officer titles — 上尉 (captain), 中尉 (lieutenant), 少尉 (second lieutenant) — with 上/中/少 ("upper/middle/junior") grading the base rank much like "senior/first/second" does for officer titles in English.

examples.hanzi: 这位上尉带领士兵们回到了基地。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi shàngwèi dàilǐng shìbīngmen huídào le jīdì.
examples.english: This captain led the soldiers back to the base.

examples.hanzi: 他从军三年后成了一名上尉。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngjūn sān nián hòu chéng le yì míng shàngwèi.
examples.english: After three years in the army, he became a captain.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 体 is a person's body.
本 (root) — the root of a person, the body; the traditional form was 體 with 骨 (bone).

example.hanzi: 锻炼身体很重要。
example.pinyin: Duànliàn shēntǐ hěn zhòngyào.
example.english: Exercising is very important.
example.fact: 体 is the simplified form of 體 and builds 身体 (body), 体育 (physical education), 体重 (weight), 体验 (experience). The same shape once served as an old variant of 笨 (bèn, clumsy), which is why 体 looks like 本 with a person.

examples.hanzi: 他的体育很好。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tǐyù hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He is good at sports.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章的体裁是小说。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng de tǐcái shì xiǎoshuō.
examples.english: The genre of this article is fiction.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
口 (mouth) — speech or assent: to say "OK". 可 is also a famous sound part: 河 hé, 歌 gē, 哥 gē, 何 hé all take their sound from it.

example.hanzi: 这份合同不可涂改。
example.pinyin: Zhè fèn hétong bùkě túgǎi.
example.english: This contract must not be altered.
example.fact: 不可 is the formal, literary counterpart of 不能 or 不要, most often seen in written rules and set idioms — 不可思议 ("inconceivable"), 不可救药 ("incurable, hopeless") — rather than in everyday spoken prohibitions.

examples.hanzi: 这里不可停车。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ bù kě tíngchē.
examples.english: Parking is not allowed here.

examples.hanzi: 想要成功,不可不努力。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎng yào chénggōng, bù kě bù nǔlì.
examples.english: If you want to succeed, you can't avoid hard work.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions applied to people: 放, 改, 政; 教 is to teach, traditionally with a rod.
孝 (xiào) is a near sound match for jiào; also in 酵 jiào.
月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); the top is an upside-down baby, so 育 is giving birth and then raising, educating.

example.hanzi: 每个孩子都应该接受良好的教育。
example.pinyin: Měi gè háizi dōu yīnggāi jiēshòu liánghǎo de jiàoyù.
example.english: Every child should receive a good education.
example.fact: 教育 combines 教 ("to teach", from a hand with a stick disciplining a child) and 育 (a mother's body with a baby growing inside, "to raise, to nurture") — literally "to teach and nurture," reflecting how the word covers both instruction and upbringing, not just schooling.

examples.hanzi: 老师的责任是教育学生,也要关心他们。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī de zérèn shì jiàoyù xuésheng, yě yào guānxīn tāmen.
examples.english: A teacher's duty is to educate students and also care about them.

examples.hanzi: 父母要对孩子进行正确的教育。
examples.pinyin: Fùmǔ yào duì háizi jìnxíng zhèngquè de jiàoyù.
examples.english: Parents should give their children the right education.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说, 话, 请; 谎 is a spoken lie.
荒 (huāng) sounds the same as 谎 huǎng except for tone; also 慌 huāng.
言 (speech) — 言 is the traditional full form of the 讠 radical for speech and language: 说, 话, 语, 请.

example.hanzi: 他说的都是谎言。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō de dōu shì huǎngyán.
example.english: Everything he said is a lie.
example.fact: 谎言 pairs 谎 ("lie", speech radical 讠 plus phonetic 荒, an exact sound match differing only in tone) with 言 ("words, speech") — literally "lying words." It names the lie itself as a noun; the everyday verb "to lie" is instead the fixed phrase 说谎, not 说谎言.

examples.hanzi: 别相信他,他一直在说谎言。
examples.pinyin: Bié xiāngxìn tā, tā yìzhí zài shuō huǎngyán.
examples.english: Don't trust him, he keeps telling lies.

examples.hanzi: 这个谎言很快就被大家发现了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège huǎngyán hěn kuài jiù bèi dàjiā fāxiàn le.
examples.english: This lie was soon discovered by everyone.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to meet is to cross paths.
禺 (yú) is close to yù; same part in 愚 yú and 偶 ǒu.
见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.

example.hanzi: 我在路上遇见了一个老朋友。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài lù shàng yùjiàn le yí gè lǎo péngyou.
example.english: I ran into an old friend on the way.
example.fact: 遇见 stresses an unplanned, chance encounter — 遇 alone already means "to run into, to encounter" — unlike 见面, which implies a planned or mutual meeting, so 遇见 rarely appears in sentences like "let's meet at 3pm."

examples.hanzi: 我昨天在火车站遇见了小学同学。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān zài huǒchēzhàn yùjiàn le xiǎoxué tóngxué.
examples.english: Yesterday I ran into an elementary school classmate at the train station.

examples.hanzi: 很高兴能在这里遇见你。
examples.pinyin: Hěn gāoxìng néng zài zhèlǐ yùjiàn nǐ.
examples.english: I'm very happy to meet you here.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — a picture of an ear; as a radical it marks hearing, as in 闻, 聪, 聊.
木 (tree) — 木 is a tree, as in 树, 桌, 林; 朵 is a cluster hanging from a branch, the measure word for flowers and clouds.

example.hanzi: 小狗的耳朵很大。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu de ěrduo hěn dà.
example.english: The puppy's ears are very big.
example.fact: 朵 is ordinarily a measure word for flowers and clouds (一朵花, "a flower"; 一朵云, "a cloud") — pairing it with 耳 ("ear") to spell "ear" is a soft, almost affectionate image, likening the shape of an ear to a small blossom.

examples.hanzi: 我的耳朵有点儿疼。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de ěrduo yǒudiǎnr téng.
examples.english: My ear hurts a little.

examples.hanzi: 他用手捂住了耳朵,因为声音太大了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng shǒu wǔ zhù le ěrduo, yīnwèi shēngyīn tài dà le.
examples.english: He covered his ears with his hands because the noise was too loud.

components.note: 世 (generation) — from 卅 (thirty): about thirty years is one generation, so an age or the world.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 世上没有十全十美的人。
example.pinyin: Shìshàng méiyǒu shí quán shí měi de rén.
example.english: There is no one in the world who is perfect in every way.
example.fact: 世上 is a shortened form of the fuller 世界上 ("in the world") — dropping 界 keeps the same meaning but leans more literary, which is why it turns up often in set phrases and sayings like 世上无难事 ("nothing in this world is too hard") rather than in everyday chit-chat.

examples.hanzi: 世上只有妈妈好。
examples.pinyin: Shìshàng zhǐ yǒu māma hǎo.
examples.english: There's no one in the world like Mom.

examples.hanzi: 世上没有后悔药,做事要想清楚。
examples.pinyin: Shìshàng méiyǒu hòuhuǐ yào, zuòshì yào xiǎng qīngchu.
examples.english: There's no medicine for regret in this world, so think clearly before acting.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 艹 here is grass over a body 死, with 廾 (two hands) laying it down — burial.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — rites and worship: 神 god, 祝 wish, 福 fortune; 礼 are ritual courtesies.

example.hanzi: 我们明天要去参加葬礼。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān yào qù cānjiā zànglǐ.
example.english: We are going to attend a funeral tomorrow.
example.fact: 葬 pictures a body being laid down among grass by two hands (艹 grass, 死 corpse, 廾 two hands) — a fairly direct image of burial — while 礼 (from 礻, "altar, ritual") adds the sense of ceremony, so 葬礼 literally reads as "burial rite."

examples.hanzi: 他昨天去参加了朋友爷爷的葬礼。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuótiān qù cānjiā le péngyou yéye de zànglǐ.
examples.english: He attended his friend's grandfather's funeral yesterday.

examples.hanzi: 葬礼上,大家都很难过。
examples.pinyin: Zànglǐ shang, dàjiā dōu hěn nánguò.
examples.english: Everyone was sad at the funeral.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 某 first named a sour tree fruit; now it means a certain, unnamed one. It sounds out 媒 méi, 煤 méi and 谋 móu.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 据说某人对这件事很不满意。
example.pinyin: Jùshuō mǒurén duì zhè jiàn shì hěn bù mǎnyì.
example.english: I heard a certain person is quite unhappy about this matter.
example.fact: 某人 deliberately withholds identity — sometimes because the speaker genuinely doesn't know who, but often in conversation because they know exactly who and are being coy or indirect about naming them, much like English "someone" said with a knowing look.

examples.hanzi: 某人在背后说了你的坏话。
examples.pinyin: Mǒu rén zài bèihòu shuō le nǐ de huàihuà.
examples.english: Someone said bad things about you behind your back.

examples.hanzi: 这是某人的东西,请你还给他。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì mǒu rén de dōngxi, qǐng nǐ huán gěi tā.
examples.english: This is somebody's belonging, please give it back to him.

components.note: 手 (hand) — two hands joined in respect: bowing and saluting; compare 扌 in 拿 and 打.

example.hanzi: 过年的时候我们去拜年。
example.pinyin: Guònián de shíhou wǒmen qù bàinián.
example.english: At New Year we go to pay New Year visits.
example.fact: 拜 is a respectful gesture: 拜年 (to pay New Year calls), 拜访 (to visit), 崇拜 (to worship), 拜托 (a polite "I'd be grateful if you'd"). 拜拜 is the casual "bye-bye".

examples.hanzi: 我们明天去拜访老师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān qù bàifǎng lǎoshī.
examples.english: Tomorrow we're going to visit the teacher.

examples.hanzi: 他向老人拜了拜。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng lǎorén bài le bài.
examples.english: He bowed to the old man.

meanings: urban area (as opposed to the countryside)

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 块; city walls were made of earth.
成 (chéng) sounds exactly like 城; also in 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng.
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 他从农村搬到城里工作。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng nóngcūn bān dào chénglǐ gōngzuò.
example.english: He moved from the countryside to the city for work.
example.fact: 城里 pairs 城 ("city, city wall") with 里 ("inside") to literally mean "inside the city walls" — a phrase that still carries a faint echo of the era when Chinese cities were physically walled, so being 城里 meant being inside the wall, as opposed to 城外 or the surrounding countryside.

examples.hanzi: 我家住在城里,上班很方便。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zhù zài chéng lǐ, shàngbān hěn fāngbiàn.
examples.english: My home is in the city, so commuting is convenient.

examples.hanzi: 城里的生活节奏比乡下快。
examples.pinyin: Chéng lǐ de shēnghuó jiézòu bǐ xiāngxia kuài.
examples.english: Life in the city moves faster than in the countryside.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
昏 (hūn, dusk) gives the exact sound; weddings were traditionally held at dusk, so the sound clue is also a meaning clue.

example.hanzi: 他们的婚礼在春天。
example.pinyin: Tāmen de hūnlǐ zài chūntiān.
example.english: Their wedding is in spring.
example.fact: 婚 is a bound form: 结婚 (to marry), 婚礼 (wedding), 离婚 (to divorce), 订婚 (to get engaged). Its sound part 昏 means dusk, because ritual weddings in ancient China were held at nightfall.

examples.hanzi: 他们打算明年结婚。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen dǎsuàn míngnián jiéhūn.
examples.english: They plan to marry next year.

examples.hanzi: 这是我的结婚证。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de jiéhūnzhèng.
examples.english: This is my marriage certificate.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — the top part, as in 和 and 秋. Memory aid: a woman (女) bending under a bundle of grain; grain plus woman gives 'bend / entrust', now 'appoint'.
女 (woman) — the bottom part and radical, as in 她 she and 妈 mom. Here it hints at a yielding, bending figure rather than a woman.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.
会 (meet, can) — simplified from 會, a lid on a container: bringing things together; hence meeting, then "can" (huì).

example.hanzi: 学校成立了一个新的委员会。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào chénglì le yí gè xīn de wěiyuánhuì.
example.english: The school established a new committee.
example.fact: 委员会 breaks down as 委员 ("committee member", from 委 "to entrust" plus 员 "member, personnel") plus 会 ("assembly") — literally "an assembly of entrusted members," a fairly transparent path from "a person entrusted with a duty" to "the body such people form."

examples.hanzi: 这个委员会每个月开一次会。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wěiyuánhuì měi ge yuè kāi yí cì huì.
examples.english: This committee holds a meeting once a month.

examples.hanzi: 他是学校学生委员会的主席。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì xuéxiào xuésheng wěiyuánhuì de zhǔxí.
examples.english: He is the chairman of the school's student committee.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.
木 (wood) — 木 is wood, as in 桌, 板; 构 first meant framing with timber.
勾 (gōu) — near sound — 构 is gòu; 勾 also sounds out 沟 gōu, 购 gòu and 够 gòu.

example.hanzi: 这家机构专门帮助失业的人。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā jīgòu zhuānmén bāngzhù shīyè de rén.
example.english: This organization specializes in helping unemployed people.
example.fact: 机构 combines 机 ("machine, mechanism") with 构 ("to construct, structure") — its earliest use centered on the physical mechanism of a device, with the abstract sense of an organization's "structure" emerging later, the same shift English makes when calling a bureaucracy a "machine."

examples.hanzi: 她在一家国际机构工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā guójì jīgòu gōngzuò.
examples.english: She works at an international organization.

examples.hanzi: 这家机构为老人提供免费服务。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jīgòu wèi lǎorén tígōng miǎnfèi fúwù.
examples.english: This organization provides free services for the elderly.

components.note: 亮 (liàng) is a sound clue for 谅 liàng and 晾 liàng; as a word it means bright, as in 月亮 moon.

example.hanzi: 天亮了，我们出发吧。
example.pinyin: Tiān liàng le, wǒmen chūfā ba.
example.english: It's light, let's set off.
example.fact: 亮 is both an adjective (bright) and a verb (to light up): 天亮 (daybreak), 亮灯 (turn on a light), 亮相 (to make an appearance). 漂亮 (piàoliang, pretty) and 响亮 (loud and clear) are common compounds.

examples.hanzi: 天亮以后，我们就出发。
examples.pinyin: Tiān liàng yǐhòu, wǒmen jiù chūfā.
examples.english: After daybreak, we'll set off.

examples.hanzi: 这间屋子很亮，我很喜欢。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiān wūzi hěn liàng, wǒ hěn xǐhuan.
examples.english: This room is bright, and I like it very much.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — grain radical — 程 first meant to measure grain, hence standard, then course and journey; also in 种, 秋, 稿.
呈 (chéng) — same sound — 程 is chéng; 呈 also sounds out 逞 chěng.
广 (building) — 广 is a building radical, as in 店, 床; 度 also sounds out 渡 dù and 镀 dù.

example.hanzi: 他对中文的了解已经达到了很高的程度。
example.pinyin: Tā duì Zhōngwén de liǎojiě yǐjīng dádào le hěn gāo de chéngdù.
example.english: His understanding of Chinese has already reached a very high level.
example.fact: 程 originally named a fixed unit for measuring grain before broadening to mean "a measured stage, a journey" (as in 过程, "process") — 程度 keeps that measuring sense alive, pairing it with 度 ("a measure, degree") to describe how far along or how much of something there is.

examples.hanzi: 我的中文程度还不够好。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de Zhōngwén chéngdù hái bú gòu hǎo.
examples.english: My level of Chinese isn't good enough yet.

examples.hanzi: 这次雨下得很大,在某种程度上影响了比赛。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì yǔ xià de hěn dà, zài mǒu zhǒng chéngdù shang yǐngxiǎng le bǐsài.
examples.english: The rain was heavy and, to some extent, affected the game.

components.note: 衤 (clothing) — 衤 is the clothing radical, as in 衣, 裤, 衬; 裙 is a skirt.
君 (jūn) — near sound — 裙 is qún; 君 also sounds out 群 qún.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 她穿着一条红色的裙子。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhe yì tiáo hóngsè de qúnzi.
example.english: She is wearing a red skirt.
example.fact: 裙子 takes the measure word 条 (used for long, narrow things like ropes and rivers) rather than the default 个 — a reminder that many everyday nouns have their own dedicated classifier that a learner has to memorize alongside the noun itself.

examples.hanzi: 这条裙子的颜色很漂亮。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo qúnzi de yánsè hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: The color of this skirt is very pretty.

examples.hanzi: 我想给女儿买一条新裙子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng gěi nǚ'ér mǎi yì tiáo xīn qúnzi.
examples.english: I want to buy a new skirt for my daughter.

components.note: 卩 (kneeling person) — a person kneeling at food 皀, about to eat: right at hand, immediately; compare 既, who has already eaten.
丬 (bed/couch, left side) — the left strip, a bed seen sideways. Dictionary story: going to bed at night, the 'future' that is sure to come; read as a memory aid.
夕 (evening) — upper part of the right side, as in 外 and 多; with 寸 (hand/inch) it frames 将 meaning 'about to / will'.

example.hanzi: 春节即将来临。
example.pinyin: Chūnjié jíjiāng láilín.
example.english: The Spring Festival is about to arrive.
example.fact: 即将 is a formal, written-register way to say "about to" — its component 即 alone already means "right away" (from a kneeling person, 卩, in front of a bowl of food, 皀, about to eat) — while casual speech reaches instead for 快要 or 马上 to express the same imminent sense.

examples.hanzi: 火车即将到站,请带好您的行李。
examples.pinyin: Huǒchē jíjiāng dào zhàn, qǐng dàihǎo nín de xíngli.
examples.english: The train is about to arrive, please take your luggage.

examples.hanzi: 新学期即将开始,孩子们都很兴奋。
examples.pinyin: Xīn xuéqī jíjiāng kāishǐ, háizimen dōu hěn xīngfèn.
examples.english: The new semester is about to begin and the kids are all excited.

components.note: 石 (stone) — marks stone and hard things, as in 破, 码, 砖; 碎 is to smash into bits.
卒 (zú) hints at the sound: 碎 suì is close to 醉 zuì and 翠 cuì.

example.hanzi: 杯子掉在地上碎了。
example.pinyin: Bēizi diào zài dìshang suì le.
example.english: The cup fell and shattered.
example.fact: 碎 describes shattered or crushed things: 碎片 (fragment), 粉碎 (smash), 碎纸 (shredded paper). At New Year, a broken dish is waved off with 岁岁平安, because 碎 and 岁 (suì, year) sound the same.

examples.hanzi: 他不小心把碗打碎了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎoxīn bǎ wǎn dǎsuì le.
examples.english: He accidentally smashed the bowl.

examples.hanzi: 这块饼干碎了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kuài bǐnggān suì le.
examples.english: This cookie is broken.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — marks vessels, as in 盒 box, 盖 lid, 盆 basin; 盘 is a plate.
舟 (boat) here stands in for 般 (bān), which hints at pán, as in 搬 bān.

example.hanzi: 桌子上有一盘水果。
example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu yì pán shuǐguǒ.
example.english: There is a plate of fruit on the table.
example.fact: 盘 is a plate or tray and the measure word for plated dishes: 一盘菜. It also counts games and records: 一盘棋 (a game of chess). 光盘 is a CD, and 盘点 means to take stock.

examples.hanzi: 我们点了一盘饺子。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen diǎn le yì pán jiǎozi.
examples.english: We ordered a plate of dumplings.

examples.hanzi: 这盘棋他下得很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè pán qí tā xiàde hěn hǎo.
examples.english: He played this game of chess very well.

components.note: 钅 (metal) — 钅 is simplified 金 (metal), as in 钱, 铁, 银; 钻 is a drill, then a diamond.
占 (zhàn) — near sound — 钻 is zuān/zuàn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 战 zhàn.
石 (stone) — a rock 口 at the foot of a cliff 厂; as a radical it marks stones and minerals, as in 破, 码, 砖, 磨.

example.hanzi: 她的婚戒上镶着一颗钻石。
example.pinyin: Tā de hūnjiè shàng xiāng zhe yì kē zuànshí.
example.english: There is a diamond set in her wedding ring.
example.fact: 钻 as a standalone verb (zuān) means "to drill, to bore through" — a diamond's extreme hardness has long made it the tool of choice for cutting other stones, so 钻石 literally names the gem by what it's used for rather than by its sparkle.

examples.hanzi: 这颗钻石又大又亮。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kē zuànshí yòu dà yòu liàng.
examples.english: This diamond is big and bright.

examples.hanzi: 他花了很多钱给妻子买钻石项链。
examples.pinyin: Tā huā le hěn duō qián gěi qīzi mǎi zuànshí xiàngliàn.
examples.english: He spent a lot of money to buy his wife a diamond necklace.

components.note: 又 (hand) — two hands pass a vessel: one gives, one receives; 授 shòu adds 扌 for "give".
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
子 (child) — 了 is usually read as a swaddled baby, like 子 without the arms. Its meanings 'finish' (了解 liǎo) and the particle le were borrowed later.

example.hanzi: 这里的天气太热了,我实在受不了。
example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de tiānqì tài rè le, wǒ shízài shòubuliǎo.
example.english: The weather here is so hot, I really can't stand it.
example.fact: 受不了 is built from 受 ("to bear, to receive") plus the negative potential infix 不 and complement 了 ("manage to") — literally "cannot manage to bear it." Swapping in 得 for 不 gives its positive twin 受得了 ("can bear it"), the same V+得/不+了 pattern behind many Chinese verb complements, like 吃得了 / 吃不了 ("can/can't finish eating").

examples.hanzi: 你一直吵,我真的受不了了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yìzhí chǎo, wǒ zhēn de shòubuliǎo le.
examples.english: You keep making noise and I really can't stand it anymore.

examples.hanzi: 这个味道太臭了,谁都受不了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèidao tài chòu le, shéi dōu shòubuliǎo.
examples.english: This smell is so bad that nobody can stand it.

components.note: 艮 (hard, stubborn) — 艮 suggests hard and stubborn; 艰 is simplified from 艱, whose 堇 (jǐn) gave the sound, with 又 now standing in for it.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) — 难 was first the name of a bird; "hard" is a borrowed use. The 又 here stands in for the traditional left part.

example.hanzi: 公司正经历一段艰难的时期。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī zhèng jīnglì yí duàn jiānnán de shíqī.
example.english: The company is going through a difficult period.
example.fact: 艰 and 难 are near-synonyms both meaning "difficult" — 难 is the common, everyday word for "hard," while 艰 mostly appears locked inside compounds (艰苦, 艰巨, 艰难) and rarely stands alone, so pairing it with the more familiar 难 helps anchor its meaning.

examples.hanzi: 刚来这座城市的时候,生活很艰难。
examples.pinyin: Gāng lái zhè zuò chéngshì de shíhou, shēnghuó hěn jiānnán.
examples.english: When I first came to this city, life was hard.

examples.hanzi: 做这个决定对他来说很艰难。
examples.pinyin: Zuò zhège juédìng duì tā lái shuō hěn jiānnán.
examples.english: Making this decision was difficult for him.

meanings: (of a matter) to be determined by

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 成功的关键在于坚持不懈。
example.pinyin: Chénggōng de guānjiàn zàiyú jiānchí bú xiè.
example.english: The key to success lies in persisting without giving up.
example.fact: 在于 splits into 在 ("at, located in") and 于 (a more literary preposition largely restricted to formal or written Chinese) — the word is essentially 在 reinforced by its own classical-register cousin, which is why 在于 sounds noticeably more formal than a casual alternative like 主要是 ("mainly is").

examples.hanzi: 这个问题的原因在于我们没有计划好。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí de yuányīn zàiyú wǒmen méiyǒu jìhuà hǎo.
examples.english: The reason for this problem lies in our lack of good planning.

examples.hanzi: 学习的关键在于每天练习。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxí de guānjiàn zàiyú měi tiān liànxí.
examples.english: The key to learning lies in daily practice.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — boundaries and surroundings: 国 country, 园 garden, 回 return; 图 is a drawn plan of a region.

example.hanzi: 请看这张地图。
example.pinyin: Qǐng kàn zhè zhāng dìtú.
example.english: Please look at this map.
example.fact: 图 is a picture or plan: 地图 (map), 图片 (picture), 图书馆 (library, "picture-book hall"). As a verb it means to seek: 图方便 (to go for convenience), and 试图 means to attempt.

examples.hanzi: 请看第三页的图。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng kàn dì-sān yè de tú.
examples.english: Please look at the picture on page three.

examples.hanzi: 他在画一张图画。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài huà yì zhāng túhuà.
examples.english: He is drawing a picture.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — actions applied to people: 放, 改, 政; 教 is to teach, traditionally with a rod.
孝 (xiào) is a near sound match for jiào; also in 酵 jiào.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and teaching: 说, 请, 课; 训 is instruction.
川 (chuān) is only a loose sound hint; 训 shares its part with 顺 shùn.

example.hanzi: 这次失败给了他一个深刻的教训。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì shībài gěi le tā yí gè shēnkè de jiàoxun.
example.english: This failure gave him a profound lesson.
example.fact: 教训 does double duty as noun ("a lesson learned the hard way") and verb ("to lecture, to scold") — a parent who 教训s a child is literally "teaching-instructing" them, and the noun sense narrowed over time to specifically mean a lesson learned through hardship, not a classroom lesson (that's 课).

examples.hanzi: 我们要从错误中吸取教训。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào cóng cuòwù zhōng xīqǔ jiàoxun.
examples.english: We should learn lessons from our mistakes.

examples.hanzi: 这件事给了我一个很大的教训。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì gěi le wǒ yí ge hěn dà de jiàoxun.
examples.english: This incident taught me a big lesson.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 土 is earth and ground, as in 地, 城, 块; 坦 is level ground, then open and frank.
旦 (dàn) — near sound — 坦 is tǎn; 旦 also sounds out 但 dàn and 担 dān.
白 (white, bright) — gives sound to 拍 pāi, 怕 pà, 伯 bó and 泊 bó. Meaning: white, clear, plain, hence "明白" understand.

example.hanzi: 他向警察坦白了一切。
example.pinyin: Tā xiàng jǐngchá tǎnbái le yíqiè.
example.english: He confessed everything to the police.
example.fact: 坦白 combines 坦 ("flat, level ground") with 白 ("clear, plain, white") — literally "level and clear," a fitting image for a confession that lays everything out openly rather than hiding anything.

examples.hanzi: 你就坦白说吧,我不会生气。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiù tǎnbái shuō ba, wǒ bú huì shēngqì.
examples.english: Just be frank, I won't get angry.

examples.hanzi: 他坦白地告诉我,他不喜欢这份工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā tǎnbái de gàosu wǒ, tā bù xǐhuan zhè fèn gōngzuò.
examples.english: He told me frankly that he doesn't like this job.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 话 speech; 议 is to discuss.
义 (yì) sounds exactly like 议; same part in 仪 yí and 蚁 yǐ.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 这位议员在演讲中提出了新的提案。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi yìyuán zài yǎnjiǎng zhōng tíchū le xīn de tí'àn.
example.english: This legislator raised a new proposal during the speech.
example.fact: 议 means "to discuss, to deliberate" (its phonetic component 义 is an exact sound match), and 员 marks a member of a body or profession, as in 演员 ("actor") or 店员 ("shopkeeper") — 议员 literally names "a member of the deliberating body," i.e. a lawmaker.

examples.hanzi: 这位议员今天要在会上发言。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yìyuán jīntiān yào zài huì shang fāyán.
examples.english: This legislator will speak at the meeting today.

examples.hanzi: 市民给议员写了一封信。
examples.pinyin: Shìmín gěi yìyuán xiě le yì fēng xìn.
examples.english: Citizens wrote a letter to the legislator.

components.note: 玉 (jade) — jade put away safely: 全 first meant flawless, pure, then whole.
囗 (enclosure) — borders and walls, as in 园 garden, 圆 round, 回 return; 囗 is the country's boundary.
玉 (jade) — treasure within the border; the traditional 國 had 或 (defended territory) inside.

example.hanzi: 这条新闻传遍了全国。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xīnwén chuánbiàn le quánguó.
example.english: This news spread across the whole country.
example.fact: 全 (from 入 "enter" plus 玉 "jade" — a treasure kept whole and undamaged) prefixes 国 ("country") to mean "the entire nation" — the same 全 + [noun] pattern reappears in this batch's own 全世界 ("the whole world"), showing how productive 全 is as a totality prefix.

examples.hanzi: 全国的学生都参加了这次考试。
examples.pinyin: Quánguó de xuésheng dōu cānjiā le zhè cì kǎoshì.
examples.english: Students all over the country took this exam.

examples.hanzi: 这家连锁店在全国有一百多家分店。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā liánsuǒdiàn zài quánguó yǒu yì bǎi duō jiā fēndiàn.
examples.english: This chain has over a hundred branches nationwide.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 心 is the heart, as in 想, 爱, 念; 慈 is a loving, kind heart.
兹 (zī) — near sound — 慈 is cí; 兹 also sounds out 磁 cí.
羊 (sheep) — 羊 is a symbol of good fortune, as in 美 and 祥; 善 is goodness and kindness, together with 口 (words).

example.hanzi: 她把大部分收入都捐给了慈善机构。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ dàbùfen shōurù dōu juān gěi le císhàn jīgòu.
example.english: She donated most of her income to charitable organizations.
example.fact: 慈善 almost always shows up attached to a following noun — 慈善机构 ("charity organization"), 慈善晚会 ("charity gala") — rather than standing alone for "charity" itself, which is instead 慈善事业 ("the charity cause") or, in casual speech, simply 捐款 ("donation").

examples.hanzi: 她经常参加慈善活动。
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngcháng cānjiā císhàn huódòng.
examples.english: She often takes part in charity events.

examples.hanzi: 他是个慈善的人,常常帮助穷人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge císhàn de rén, chángcháng bāngzhù qióngrén.
examples.english: He is a kind-hearted person who often helps the poor.

components.note: 食 (food) — eating and meals: 饭, 饿, 饱 (as 饣); 餐 is a meal.
饣 (food, simplified 食) — eating and meals: 饭, 饿, 饱; 馆 is an inn or restaurant, a place that serves food.
官 (guān) sounds exactly like 馆 apart from tone; also in 管 guǎn.

example.hanzi: 我们晚上去那家新开的餐馆吃饭吧。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshang qù nà jiā xīn kāi de cānguǎn chīfàn ba.
example.english: Let's go eat at that newly opened restaurant tonight.
example.fact: 餐馆 is one of several near-synonyms for "restaurant" alongside 饭店 and 饭馆 — 餐馆 leans slightly more formal or Western in flavor (西餐馆, "Western restaurant"), while 饭店 in Mainland usage can also mean "hotel," a common trap for learners who assume it always means "restaurant."

examples.hanzi: 这家餐馆的饺子特别好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cānguǎn de jiǎozi tèbié hǎochī.
examples.english: The dumplings at this restaurant are especially delicious.

examples.hanzi: 他在一家小餐馆里当服务员。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā xiǎo cānguǎn lǐ dāng fúwùyuán.
examples.english: He works as a waiter in a small restaurant.

components.note: 讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and agreements, as in 说, 请, 计; 订 is to book or settle by word.
丁 (dīng) hints at the sound: 订 dìng is close, as in 钉 dīng and 顶 dǐng.

example.hanzi: 我想订一张去北京的机票。
example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng dìng yì zhāng qù Běijīng de jīpiào.
example.english: I'd like to book a flight ticket to Beijing.
example.fact: 订 is to book or order: 订票, 订餐, 订阅 (to subscribe). It also means to fix an agreement: 订婚 (to get engaged), 订合同 (to sign a contract). Don't confuse it with 定 (dìng, to settle).

examples.hanzi: 我订了一间双人房。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ dìng le yì jiān shuāngrénfáng.
examples.english: I booked a double room.

examples.hanzi: 我们订了一个蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dìng le yí gè dàngāo.
examples.english: We ordered a cake.

components.note: 罒 (net) — 罒 is a net, as in 罚, 置; 罗 is a net, and is mostly seen in 罗马 Rome.
马 (horse) — a galloping horse. As a radical it marks horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive. It gives sound to 妈 mā, 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.

example.hanzi: 罗马是意大利的首都。
example.pinyin: Luómǎ shì Yìdàlì de shǒudū.
example.english: Rome is the capital of Italy.
example.fact: 罗马 is a phonetic transliteration with no real connection to its characters' own meanings (罗 "net," 马 "horse") — the characters were picked purely for their sound, the same strategy Chinese uses for most foreign place names.

examples.hanzi: 罗马有很多古老的建筑。
examples.pinyin: Luómǎ yǒu hěn duō gǔlǎo de jiànzhù.
examples.english: Rome has many ancient buildings.

examples.hanzi: 我们明年夏天打算去罗马旅游。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngnián xiàtiān dǎsuàn qù Luómǎ lǚyóu.
examples.english: We plan to travel to Rome next summer.

components.note: 大 (person) — a man with a hairpin 一 on his head, a grown man; 夫 also gives 扶 fú and 肤 fū.

example.hanzi: 他是一位好丈夫。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi hǎo zhàngfu.
example.english: He is a good husband.
example.fact: 夫 is rarely free-standing but common in compounds: 夫妻 (married couple), 丈夫 (husband), 夫人 (madam), 功夫 (kung fu). 大夫 is read dàifu (doctor) when colloquial and dàfū (a senior official) in history.

examples.hanzi: 她的丈夫是医生。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zhàngfu shì yīshēng.
examples.english: Her husband is a doctor.

examples.hanzi: 他是个农夫，每天都在地里干活。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè nóngfū, měitiān dōu zài dì lǐ gànhuó.
examples.english: He is a farmer who works in the fields every day.
